headline: Highest risk is Dify’s broad server-side execution and shared datastore, but the pair’s direct interaction is undocumented and B is network-isolated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge-base files and shared datastore content, so if spring-integration-samples is used as a manual copy-paste or file bridge, prompt injection is possible. B has no documented input surface or network egress, so the pathway is weaker and likely manual rather than automatic.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples content is copied into Dify prompts or knowledge files
IF Dify treats uploaded file text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted sample text into prompts
Mark uploaded files as untrusted in operator workflow
Add a review step before any file is indexed
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches conversation logs and knowledge-base content and can write/read the filesystem, while spring-integration-samples is documented as network-egress none. The pair does not show a shared workspace or third-party upload path for B, so leakage risk is limited and mostly local to Dify’s stored data.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace
IF Dify stores sensitive conversation logs in a shared directory
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Restrict Dify file access to a dedicated directory
Purge conversation logs after use
Confirm B remains network-disabled

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has broad filesystem and subprocess capability, but spring-integration-samples is not documented as runnable and has no write or network capabilities listed. Without a shared mutable target or locking issue, direct capability conflict is unlikely; uncertainty stays low because B’s operational surface is sparse.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples is made runnable in the same directory as Dify outputs
IF both agents write to the same files without external locking
mitigations: Use separate output directories
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
Run one agent at a time for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate agent/workflow outputs that downstream tools may trust, and spring-integration-samples is a sample repository that could be treated as authoritative example code or configuration. If Dify’s output is fed into B-style workflows without verification, errors can cascade across multiple work products even though B itself has no action authority documented.
conditions: IF Dify output is used as input to a downstream workflow without validation
IF sample code or configuration from spring-integration-samples is treated as authoritative
mitigations: Add human review before reuse of generated output
Require schema validation on downstream inputs
Label sample repository content as non-authoritative
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, model-provider API keys, and tool credentials, while spring-integration-samples has no documented sensitive-data handling or residency controls. The mismatch is mainly that Dify may retain sensitive operational data; B is not shown to add a separate regulated-data burden, so compliance risk is limited.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify conversation logs or knowledge files
IF retention or residency requirements apply to those logs
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Dify
Rotate exposed tool credentials
Set short retention on logs where available
requires-engineering: configure residency and deletion controls
